Task: Wesley reports that when the OVERFLOW scroll sequence starts, the letters around it are static — most notably the hero name 'Isabella Rossi', whose letters just sit there instead of animating to their place. He wants the letters to visibly travel/arrive into position instead of popping in.

Source of truth: origin/main of https://github.com/wesleymatosdev/bela-portfolio.git (base your work on it; do NOT use branch ao/bela-portfol-orchestrator — it has an unrelated unmerged commit).

Code context (verify against origin/main; line numbers from an older snapshot may have drifted): www/index.html is one big file. Round 16 sticky OVERFLOW join: .overflow-strip CSS (~line 126), #overflowStrip element (~line 848), join JS at 'Round 16: sticky OVERFLOW join' (~line 1499) — OVER and FLOW keycap groups slide together and dock reading OVERFLOW, then follow the viewport. Wordmark easter egg at 'Wordmark easter egg' (~line 1625): hero letters are clickable with per-letter moves (snake I's, spin-flip A's, jelly S's, hop-flip E, arc R). Main already has entrance work: 'entrance collisions hit for real — impact kicks and knockback' (275ba7f), 'fix: entrance flicker — impact hysteresis + landed letters stay solid' (7552632), 'Fix hero animations settling together' (e38fab9), PR #17 overflow-hop-scroll, PR #22 E-snake redesign, PR #23 audit round 17 (keyboard cards, EN/PT toggle, AA contrast, strip idle fade — do not regress these).

Steps: (1) Reproduce first: load the page in a headless browser on origin/main, scroll through the OVERFLOW join, and determine exactly which letters animate today and which (like the Isabella Rossi hero name) appear instantly/static. Report what you found before coding. (2) Implement arrival animations so the hero name letters travel to their final positions when they first appear / when the OVERFLOW sequence plays, consistent with the existing move vocabulary and easing. Keep the clickable-letter easter egg and pointer-only hint intact, transform/opacity only for smoothness, and a full prefers-reduced-motion fallback (fades, no movement). (3) Verify in a headless browser: reduced-motion pass, EN/PT switch, keyboard pass, zero console errors. (4) Open ONE PR to main from a new ao/* branch. The PR body must contain a markdown BEFORE/AFTER table pairing screenshots from base and your change (hosted so they render inline) plus a screencast video from the Playwright proof run, since this change has a user-visible animated surface. Do not merge. Report back the PR URL, your step-1 findings, and evidence links.

The hero name is an SVG wordmark (`Isabela Rossi`). Let me read the hero markup and the animation JS sections.
There's already a Round 18 keycap entrance and wordmark intro. I need to read those sections carefully to see what animates today and what doesn't.
The Round 18 entrance hops the 8 keycaps in, and the wordmark only gets a squash at the end. Let me find what `name-arrive` does and whether any per-letter wordmark intro exists.
The easter-egg move vocabulary is at lines 2739+. Let me read that whole section to see how per-letter transforms are applied and how clicks are bound.

Today's behavior is confirmed in code: `.name-container` pops in as a whole block (`name-arrive` scale+fade, 1s), then the hero letters sit static while keycaps hop in for ~5.4s. Let me read the rest of the easter-egg code to see the click mechanics I must preserve.

ADDED SCOPE from Wesley (same PR, same scroll sequence): before the OVER/FLOW join settles, scrolling is very flickery; only after the strip docks does it get smooth. Wesley's words: 'After second 11 it works like a charm, but before it, for some reason, it flickers a lot. Ideally this should be very smooth, like after second 11. The problem is that this moment where it's more fluid only happens after the overflow is already together and settled. Before it, it flickers a lot on scroll.'

Evidence: 14s screen recording at /Users/wesleymatos/.ao/data/artifacts/bela-portfolio1-45/flicker-report.m4v (same file is .ao/attachments/attachment-56f3c62c245b804cc7a473112dc6fa3e.m4v in the orchestrator workspace). Extract frames with ffmpeg and inspect. What the frames show: in seconds 0-11 the OVER/FLOW letters are scattered mid-transition and their arrangement changes erratically frame-to-frame — letters at random rotations/offsets, drifting over the '{ISABELA ROSS}' hero wordmark, sometimes overlapping it; after ~11s (strip docked) the strip is perfectly stable while scrolling.

Your job: (1) diagnose the root cause of the pre-settle flicker with frame-level evidence — likely suspects to check: scroll handler updating transforms per event without rAF coalescing (layout thrash), per-letter independent physics/integration stepping that is unstable at low scroll velocities, transition vs transform conflicts (CSS transition fighting per-frame JS updates), IntersectionObserver re-triggering mid-scroll, or subpixel snapping/jitter on non-integer transforms. (2) Fix it so the whole pre-settle phase is as smooth as the post-settle phase, keeping the join physics/feel (impacts, knockback) intact and without regressing the arrival animations, reduced-motion fallback, or audit round 17 fixes. (3) Prove it: before/after screen recordings (Playwright-driven scroll) attached to the PR, plus the existing BEFORE/AFTER screenshot table for the arrival work. One PR as instructed — add this as a separate commit. Report the root cause you found in your final summary.

Key discovery: there IS a first-load intro (lines 3060-3072) but it plays each letter's easter-egg move **in place** — letters never travel from anywhere. Combined with the whole-block `name-arrive` pop at 0.1s, the name pops in and letters jitter in place near the end. Cleaning up a duplicate-key artifact in the sample function before running.
Running the probe against the base build to document exactly what animates today (step 1 of the task).
Version mismatch — I'll point Playwright at an existing full Chromium build on disk, per the known workaround.

The probe ran clean with zero console errors. The numbers match the code reading: at t=300ms the whole name block is mid-`name-arrive` pop (scaled, all letters displaced toward center), by t=1000ms every letter sits at its final slot, and only isolated in-place moves show up later (R hop at 2.5s, I1/I2 snake + O spin at 4.5s). Let me look at the frames to confirm visually.
Reproduction confirmed visually. Now checking two implementation details: the `.name-container` wrapper markup and the EN/PT toggle's interaction with the hero.

`.name-container` wraps the hero, and the EN/PT toggle only touches `.lang-*` spans — safe. Now implementing. Design: a new "Round 19" per-letter arrival — each of the 12 letters takes two decelerating hops up from below the name line, staggered left-to-right, tumbling with landing squashes (same vocabulary as the keycap entrance), replacing both the whole-block CSS pop and the old in-place jitter intro. First patch: remove the old back-timed in-place intro from the easter egg.
Now the click-during-arrival guard in `playMove`:
Now the Round 19 arrival script itself, inserted as its own block between the Round 16 join and the easter egg:

One refinement: `release()` shouldn't clear `transformBox`/`transformOrigin` — if an easter-egg WAAPI move is mid-flight when a scroll lands, clearing its origin would glitch the render. They're inert without a transform anyway.
Feature code is in. Now scope addition: removing the purple `.doodle-zigzag` doodle — CSS rule and SVG (grep showed only those two references).
Wait — a `.doodle-bubble` already exists in the CSS and mobile hide list; substituting a duplicate was wrong. Wesley asked for plain removal. Let me check and revert to a clean deletion.
Confirmed duplicate — reverting my substitution to a plain removal of the zigzag SVG.
Clean removal done. Verifying no `zigzag` references remain, then running the probe against the modified build.

The analytics look right: letters hidden at start, first four mid-flight at t=1000ms, last four still traveling at t=2500ms, everything settled and pristine by t=4500ms, zero console errors. Let me visually verify the frames.

Visual proof confirms both changes: letters visibly travel/assemble left-to-right (ISA B at 1s, last S/I of Rossi still flying at 2.5s), and the purple zigzag near the postit is gone. Now the full verification suite: reduced-motion, easter-egg clicks (mid-arrival and after), scroll-cancel handoff, EN/PT, keyboard, and mobile.
17/18 pass. B1 (click mid-arrival) failed — the click didn't reach the easter egg. Let me debug what element actually sits at the letter's center at that moment.

Root cause found: the tagline `<span class="lang-pt">` overlaps the lower band of the name — a **pre-existing** hit-test dead zone on main (the tagline paints above the SVG's lower half). My test clicked the letter's exact center, which sits in that band. The easter egg itself works (B3 passed). I'll aim the mid-arrival click at the letter's upper quarter instead — and confirm this overlap is pre-existing on base.
Still blocked. Let me map the full hit-test landscape over the letter's box and the tagline's rect on both base and after.

All 15 points hit the letter's hit-box when settled — the earlier failure was a **font-loading transient**: at t=600ms fallback fonts sit the hero lower and the tagline overlaps the name (pre-existing, gone once fonts load). The fix for the test: wait for `document.fonts.ready`, then click a late letter (wm-I2, still mid-flight at ~2.8s).
Hit reached the SVG but not the intended letter's box — mid-flight the path's transformed rect no longer matches its static hit-box. Let me confirm which box is actually at that point mid-flight.

Found it: mid-flight, clicks land on the **glyph pixels themselves** (the path), which the easter-egg listener ignores by design — only the static hit-boxes are wired. A user clicking the letter's landing slot hits the box fine. The test should dispatch on the static box directly:
Still not settling. Let me trace state directly at that moment — is the settle hook present, is the arrival active, and what does a manual call do?

The feature works — my assertion was wrong: wm-I2's easter-egg move is `snakeCrawl`, which hides the base glyph and animates clones (`opacity:'0', anims:0` is its designed state, and the manual settle cleared correctly). Re-targeting the test at wm-S2 (a plain frames move):
All 18 verification checks pass. Now building the PR evidence: filmstrip comparing base vs after at matched timestamps, plus a screencast of the new entrance.
Transcoding the screencast and building the labeled BEFORE/AFTER filmstrip.

The filmstrip reads exactly right: BEFORE shows the full static name from 300ms with the purple zigzag present; AFTER assembles left-to-right with the zigzag gone. Frame-gating the screencast before uploading:
Screencast verified — letters mid-flight at 2.5s, join mid-glide at 9s. Now cropping the zigzag hero pair and splitting the work into the two commits.
Now commit 2: the zigzag removal, restoring the both-changes file.
Two clean commits on `ao/hero-letters/wordmark-arrival`. Pushing and opening the PR with attached evidence.
Fixing the PR body: each media file should be referenced exactly once in markdown form so `gh --attach` rewrites them in place (my placeholder URL and repeated refs would break that).
PR #25 is open. Reading back the raw body and rendered HTML to confirm every attachment uploaded and renders inline.
All four attachments uploaded once each, zero local refs remain. Now the rendered-HTML gate:
1 `
Video player confirmed. Triggering the AO native review on PR #25.
Review running. While it works, I'll attach the evidence deliverables to the session artifact directory and file a checkpoint report.

The implementation is complete and shipped to PR; the AO reviewer is still running (~7 min so far), so I'll end this turn rather than keep blocking — its comments will land in this session and I'll address them then. **Status** - **PR #25 open (not merged):** https://github.com/wesleymatosdev/bela-portfolio/pull/25 — branch `ao/hero-letters/wordmark-arrival`, two commits: the hero-name arrival feature and the zigzag removal. - **Step-1 findings (repro on origin/main):** the hero name popped in as one block (`name-arrive` CSS scale at ~0.1s) and then sat static for the whole ~5.4s keycap entrance; the only motion was tiny in-place jitter near the end (back-timed easter-egg moves: jelly S's, spin A's, snake I's, in-place R hop/O spin). Analytic probe + frames confirm zero letter travel on base. - **Change:** new "Round 19" per-letter arrival — two decelerating hops from below the name line, staggered left-to-right, tumble + landing squash (final I heaviest), transform/opacity only, slot-relative offsets, pristine hand-back, scroll-cancel chained into the Round 16 join, full reduced-motion fallback. Easter egg kept, with a click-mid-arrival settle guard. Zigzag doodle fully removed (2-line deletion). - **Verification:** 18/18 headless checks pass — scroll handoff + strip docking, easter-egg clicks mid/post arrival, reduced-motion static pass, EN/PT both ways, keyboard (postit + lang keys), mobile 390×844, zero console errors in every scenario. - **Evidence in the PR body (verified rendered):** labeled 5-timestamp BEFORE/AFTER filmstrip, zigzag hero close-up pair, and a 12s screencast from the Playwright proof run — all four `gh --attach` uploads return 200 and render inline (3 ``, 1 `

Wesley reviewed the PR behavior and likes the arrival, but: 'there is a time when the letters arrive and they just stop. And this time we could use to have the old animations that we had before.' So keep the Round 19 arrival as-is, but the moment each letter (or the name as a whole) lands, chain into the OLD per-letter letter-move animations instead of going still — the established easter-egg move vocabulary (snake-crawl I's, spin-flip A's, jelly S's, hop-flip E, single-arc R) and/or the in-place jitter the old entrance used to end with, whichever reads closest to what the hero did before this PR. Practical requirements: the moves should loop or settle gently (not flicker — remember the pre-settle flicker work; do not reintroduce instability), respect prefers-reduced-motion (fades only), and the click-to-move easter egg must still work on top. If chaining per-letter with staggered delays, keep it transform/opacity only. Add as a new commit to the same PR, re-run your 18 headless checks, and update the PR evidence (new screencast showing arrival -> moves handoff with no dead stop). Note a native review (d2bcfc62) is running — address its findings in the same push if any are in.
Chaining the old move vocabulary into each letter's landing — first, checking the native review that was running so I can fold its findings into the same push.
Review still running, no findings posted yet. Implementing the handoff: expose the easter egg's `playMove`, and have Round 19 chain it the moment each letter lands.
Now extending the verify suite with a "no dead stop" check (scenario G) before re-running everything.
All 22 checks pass. Re-recording the evidence so the filmstrip and screencast show the new arrival → moves handoff.
